rationale: Evidence: R2A iteration 1 (the R1 candidate) still ended all 60 trials off_track with 0 finishes. Progress was 0.04 to 0.14, each trial logged exactly one line_loss_event, and max_error was 0.0607 to 0.0615 on every track. That is just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, and it is nearly identical across tracks and seeds. Lowering kp from 3.0 to 2.0 and raising sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 changed max_error very little, so gain and footprint are not the main cause. The fixed left/right motor mismatch is a constant turning bias. A proportional-only controller settles at a steady offset of roughly bias/(kp*gain) from the line, and that offset is a plausible route to reaching the 0.06 m limit. Integral action removes that steady offset. Hypothesis H3: the robot drifts to a steady offset set by the motor mismatch, and ki will pull it back toward the centre line. Change: add ki = 0.4, a moderate value that stays well inside the +/-2 integral limit. I am keeping every other value from R1 (kp 2.0, kd 0.15, sensor_size 0.016, base_speed 1.4, line_loss last_direction) so the race isolates the integral effect. I am not changing line_loss yet, because the Evaluator asked for it only if line loss persists after this test. Expected result if H3 holds: max_error falls well under 0.06, line_loss_events drops toward 0, and progress rises above 0.5 on the oval and s-bend. If max_error stays near 0.061 with ki in place, the next step is to test line_loss = search_left or search_right, and then to check whether the first 0.5 s is the failure point. Measurements wanted: max_error and rms_error over time, line_loss_events, progress per track, steering_oscillation (to check that the integral term does not add jitter), and completion_time.
